title: Cell Imbalance Detected
shortDescription: One or more cells in the M18 pack have drifted outside the acceptable voltage window.
fullDescription:
M18 Redlithium High Output packs use 5S or 10S cell configurations. The internal BMS monitors each series group and flags BMS-01 when the spread between the highest and lowest cell exceeds ~150 mV. Imbalance develops from uneven cell aging or a single weak cell pulling the pack down during discharge.

The Super Charger includes a balance charge mode that can partially recover small imbalances; larger spreads indicate a failed cell that requires warranty replacement.

causes.cause: Deep discharge from long storage at empty

symptoms: Fuel gauge drops quickly under load

fixSteps.title: Attempt rebalance
fixSteps.instruction: Leave pack on the Milwaukee Super Charger overnight — its balance cycle may recover small spreads.

fixSteps.title: Warranty claim
fixSteps.instruction: If imbalance persists, submit an RMA through Milwaukee support — 5-year battery warranty covers replacement.

whenToCallPro: Do not open the pack — cells pose a fire risk. Use Milwaukee warranty.

faq.a: No — cells are spot-welded and require proper BMS programming. Warranty replace.

title: Overcharge Protection Triggered
shortDescription: Cell voltage exceeded safe upper limit during charge.
fullDescription: Each series group is limited to 4.20 V per cell. BMS-02 indicates a cell reached 4.25+ V during charge — the BMS cut off charging immediately. Persistent BMS-02 reflects cell damage and requires pack replacement.

fixSteps.title: Try another charger
fixSteps.instruction: Verify on a second known-good Milwaukee charger.

affectedModels: Milwaukee M18 Redlithium packs, any capacity
whenToCallPro: Always — never attempt to open a lithium pack.

faq.a: Yes — BMS prevents thermal runaway. Don't defeat it.

title: Over-Discharge Protection
shortDescription: Cell voltage fell below 2.5 V under load — pack locked out.
fullDescription: If pack voltage falls below 2.5 V per cell the BMS disables discharge permanently to prevent copper dissolution in the anodes. Recovery requires the Milwaukee Super Charger's revive mode — but some over-discharged packs never recover full capacity.

causes.cause: High-load surge deeper than BMS could interrupt

fixSteps.title: Super Charger revive
fixSteps.instruction: Place pack on M18 Super Charger (48-59-1808) — it attempts low-current trickle to revive.

fixSteps.title: Warranty
fixSteps.instruction: If revival fails, submit warranty claim.

videoSearchQuery: Milwaukee battery dead revive super charger

faq.q: Can I trickle charge with a universal charger?
faq.a: Never — this is how packs catch fire. Milwaukee charger only.

title: Over-Temperature During Discharge
shortDescription: Pack internal temperature exceeded safe limit.
fullDescription: M18 HO packs trip above ~70 °C cell temperature. Common during sustained high-current work (chainsaw, leaf blower, circular saw) on hot days. Pack locks out until it cools below ~50 °C.

fixSteps.title: Rotate packs
fixSteps.instruction: Use 2-3 packs in rotation for heavy tools.

whenToCallPro: Only if over-temp trips happen at low load.

faq.q: Can I force a cold pack?
faq.a: Don't — letting it cool naturally is fastest and safest.

title: Cell Short-Circuit Fault
shortDescription: Internal cell short detected — pack permanently disabled.
fullDescription: BMS-05 is the most serious pack fault — an internal cell has shorted. The BMS permanently disables the pack to prevent thermal runaway. Do not attempt to use, charge, or open this pack — bring to a Milwaukee service center or hazardous waste recycling.

fixSteps.title: Isolate pack
fixSteps.instruction: Place in a metal container away from combustibles.

fixSteps.title: Contact Milwaukee
fixSteps.instruction: Milwaukee provides shipping materials for warranty return.

affectedModels: Any M18 pack after drop or internal failure

faq.a: Never — use Call2Recycle drop-off or Milwaukee service center.

title: BMS Communication Fault
fullDescription: The data pin between pack and tool/charger carries SOC, temperature and fault data. BMS-06 flags when this stream is interrupted. Usually a dirty contact or bent pin.

fixSteps.title: Clean terminals
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe pack and tool terminals with contact cleaner.

fixSteps.title: Inspect pins
fixSteps.instruction: Look for bent pins in pack terminal block.

faq.a: No — the BMS is sealed and not re-programmable.

title: Over-Current Protection
shortDescription: Pack drew more current than its rating allows.
fullDescription: HO/Forge packs are rated for 1000+ A peak; older XC2.0 packs much less. Using an XC2.0 pack on a table saw (2736) or large circular saw trips BMS-07. Use an HO or Forge pack for high-draw tools.
symptoms: Pack cuts out instantly under load

fixSteps.title: Use larger pack
fixSteps.instruction: Fit an HO 6.0Ah or Forge pack for high-draw tools.

affectedModels: M18 CP1.5, XC2.0 on heavy tools
videoSearchQuery: Milwaukee battery over current HO pack

faq.a: Forge 12Ah or HO 8Ah/12Ah for sustained rips.

title: Cold Temperature Lockout
shortDescription: Pack temperature below 0 °C — charging blocked to protect cells.
fullDescription:
Lithium cells plate metallic lithium when charged below freezing, causing permanent capacity loss and safety risk. BMS-08 locks charging until pack reaches 0 °C.

Tool use (discharge) is permitted but capacity is reduced in cold.
symptoms: Charger shows fault on cold pack

fixSteps.title: Warm pack
fixSteps.instruction: Bring pack indoors for 30+ minutes before charging.

faq.q: Can I use pack in cold?

title: Pack Identification Failure
shortDescription: Tool cannot recognize pack as authentic Milwaukee.
fullDescription: Third-party 'replacement' M18 batteries often fail authentication. BMS-09 means the data signature does not match Milwaukee's expected pack profile. Use genuine Milwaukee packs only.

fixSteps.title: Use genuine Milwaukee pack
fixSteps.instruction: Aftermarket packs may damage tools and void warranty.

affectedModels: Newer M18 Fuel tools reject non-OEM packs

faq.a: Some do, but risk tool damage, fire, and voided warranty.

title: Hot Charge Lockout
shortDescription: Pack too hot to charge safely.
fullDescription: Charging lithium above ~45 °C accelerates aging. BMS-10 blocks charge until pack cools below threshold. Commonly seen when pulling a pack off a heavy tool and immediately placing on charger.

fixSteps.title: Cool pack
fixSteps.instruction: Rest pack in shade 15-20 min before charging.

affectedModels: Any M18 pack after heavy use
videoSearchQuery: Milwaukee pack too hot to charge

faq.q: Does Super Charger cool the pack?
faq.a: Yes — includes active cooling fan to allow faster charge safely.
